name: Winged eyeliner for tilt

card.summary: Extending liner outward and upward to suggest a more tilted outer eye corner; a makeup technique with no studies on its effect on perceived tilt.
card.note: No studies of the technique's effect on perceived canthal tilt were found.

quick.overview:
Winged eyeliner is a makeup technique in which the line along the upper lashes is extended past the outer corner of the eye. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to imitate a positive canthal tilt, an outer eye corner sitting higher than the inner.

The technique is a long-standing makeup style. No published research was found on whether it changes how tilted the eyes look.
quick.mechanism: A dark line is drawn along the upper lash line and flicked outward and upward, so the eye is visually extended in that direction. The result is an optical illusion created with pigment.
quick.risks: Eyeliner is a standard cosmetic. Product quality varies by region, and the FDA has described traditional kohl as unsafe over lead concerns. Winged liner is typically worn with ordinary pencil or liquid liners.

lead: Winged eyeliner is a makeup technique in which the line along the upper lashes is extended past the outer corner of the eye into a flick, with the wing running about halfway toward the end of the eyebrow.[1] People use it to make the outer eye corner look higher and the eye look longer and more lifted, an effect looksmaxxing communities describe as imitating a positive canthal tilt, where the outer corner sits above the inner.

The look works with pigment rather than anatomy. Eyeliner can create the look of a wider or smaller eye depending on where and how it is drawn, so a line directed up and out draws the eye's outline in that direction.[1] A related style, cat eye, uses a thicker wing that runs along both the top and bottom lash lines.[1]

Eyeliner is a long-standing cosmetic, worn since ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia and refreshed in the 1960s with bold liquid-liner graphics.[1] Researchers have not published studies of how winged liner changes perceived canthal tilt or attractiveness; the technique is documented through makeup practice and community discussion. Canthal tilt itself is a term used in these communities, while Wikipedia's page on the canthus covers the eye-corner anatomy and landmarks without a tilt definition.[2]
infobox: Liquid, pencil, gel, felt-tip and others

paras: Eyeliner is sold as liquid, powder pencil, wax pencil, kohl, gel, cake, shimmer and felt-tip products.[1] Dark lines around the eyes have an ancient history, with Egyptians using materials such as copper ore and antimony, and the lines were worn for looks and sun protection.[1] In the 1960s liquid liner produced bold graphic lines associated with designer Mary Quant.[1]
Winged liner defines the upper lid and extends into a wing; cat eye is similar but with a thicker wing along upper and lower lashes.[1]

On looksmax.org, canthal tilt is a common topic in eye-area discussions. Related threads discuss lifting the outer brow area by surgery to give a more tilted, alert look, with some users saying results can be good and others disliking them.[3] Makeup wings are part of the same interest in tilting the outer eye; much of the forum material on tilting the eye focuses on surgical routes.
For tight lining, which places liner against the waterline, waterproof eyeliner is preferred because of the sensitive membranes of the eye.[1]

timeline.event: Egyptians and Mesopotamians wear dark lines around the eyes, using materials such as copper ore and antimony.[1]
Liquid liner creates bold graphic lines in fashion makeup, associated with Mary Quant.[1]

lore.intro: Canthal tilt is a core eye-area concept on looksmax.org, where members discuss ways to achieve a more upturned outer corner.[3]

claims.claim: A positive canthal tilt makes the eye area look more attractive and alert
claims.believers: Members describe an upward-tilted outer corner as giving a 'more awake and dominant eye region' and discuss brow-lift surgery to get it.[3]
claims.experts: No published studies in the sources examine winged liner or tilt for perceived attractiveness.

claims.claim: Winged liner can imitate a positive tilt
claims.believers: Makeup users apply an upward flick to make the outer corner appear higher.
claims.experts: No published studies have tested the effect of winged eyeliner on perceived eye tilt; eyeliner placement is described as changing perceived eye width and size.[1]

chain: Liner drawn along the upper lash line
Line flicked outward and upward past the outer corner
Eye outline is extended upward at the outside
Eyes look more tilted and lifted
angle.text: The wing is a temporary, makeup-based way to change how the outer eye corner reads. People apply it so the eye appears longer and the outer corner higher, and remove it with makeup remover afterwards.
